title: TabularMath: Evaluating Computational Extrapolation in Tabular Learning via Program-Verified Synthesis
abstract: arXiv:2602.02523v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Standard tabular benchmarks reward interpolation: predicting values inside the data manifold, where local statistical smoothing works. However, much high-value tabular data, from pricing and financial rules to physical simulation, is produced by deterministic computations rather than noisy relationships. Can tabular models move from statistical interpolation to computational extrapolation, returning exact answers even beyond the range seen in training? We introduce TabularMath, a benchmark of 114 deterministic computations (233,472 rows) compiled from GSM8K and AIME problems into verified programs. We evaluate nine tabular methods, closed-form and symbolic regression baselines, and in-context learning with GPT-OSS-120B. On regression metrics, TabPFN v2.5 looks excellent: with 128 rows its median $R^2$ is 0.999 in-distribution, and it is the only tabular method whose median $R^2$ stays positive (0.76) when nearly every answer ex

translated_title: TabularMath：通过程序验证合成评估表格学习中的计算外推能力
translated_abstract: 标准的表格基准奖励的是插值，即预测数据流形内部的值，此时局部统计平滑是有效的。然而，许多高价值的表格数据，从定价和金融规则到物理模拟，都是由确定性计算而非噪声关系产生的。表格模型能否从统计插值走向计算外推，即使在训练中未见过的范围之外也能返回精确答案？我们提出了TabularMath，这是一个包含114个确定性计算（233,472行）的基准，这些计算由GSM8K和AIME问题编译为经过验证的程序。我们评估了九种表格方法、闭式解与符号回归基线，以及使用GPT-OSS-120B的上下文学习。在回归指标上，TabPFN v2.5表现极为出色：仅用128行数据，其分布内中位数R²达到0.999，并且当几乎每个答案超出训练范围时，它是唯一一个中位数R²仍保持为正（0.76）的表格方法。
tldr: 本文提出TabularMath基准，将GSM8K和AIME问题编译为114个经程序验证的确定性计算，用以评估表格模型从统计插值到计算外推的能力，发现TabPFN v2.5在分布内中位数R²高达0.999，且是唯一在超出训练范围时中位数R²仍保持正值（0.76）的表格方法。
en_tdlr: TabularMath is a program-verified benchmark of 114 deterministic computations compiled from GSM8K and AIME problems that tests whether tabular models can perform computational extrapolation beyond the training range, showing that TabPFN v2.5 achieves a median in-distribution R² of 0.999 and is the only tabular method whose median R² stays positive (0.76) under extrapolation.
